normals_from_depth — 3D range_image op

• Data kinds: depth → normalmap

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.normals_from_depth(depth, fx=None, fy=None, cx=None, cy=None, orient_to_camera=True, spacing=None) (to call the implementation directly, import range_image; range_image.normals_from_depth(depth, fx=None, fy=None, cx=None, cy=None, orient_to_camera=True, spacing=None); from the registry, ops3d.get("normals_from_depth"))

Usage

Organized depth → oriented unit normals (H,W,3). The cross product of the 3-D points of neighbouring pixels (using the grid structure, O(HW)).

Perspective with fx,fy given, orthographic otherwise. orient_to_camera=True unifies the normal signs to face the camera (origin).

★A different function with the same name exists in the 1-line facade. fullseye.normals_from_depth is (depth, K, smooth=0), the perspective version where K is required; this one (via fullseye.ledger = range_image) is the orthographic version that takes no K. If you learn how to call one, calling the other one the same way raises TypeError (measured 2026-09-08).

★spacing=(dy, dx) is the real size of a pixel in orthographic mode. The default None means "1 pixel = 1 unit", and passing an anisotropic grid (e.g. columns 0.05 mm × rows 0.5 mm) as is silently shifts the slopes —— measured: the x component was off by 20 times (= 1/dx times), with neither an exception nor a warning. If you know the real size, always pass it. In perspective mode (fx/fy given) the focal length determines the real size, so it is ignored. ★When passing spacing, set orient_to_camera=False. In orthographic mode the "camera" is a makeshift placed at the origin (top-left, depth 0); entering real sizes changes its position relative to the surface, and the sign may flip (measured: on a plane with slope 0.1, orient_to_camera=False matches the ground truth x=-0.0995, while True gives +0.0995). If you need the orientation, align it in a later stage in a coordinate system where the line of sight is defined.

Normals come from cross products of neighbouring pixels, so both axes need neighbours. With H<2 or W<2 there is no 2nd tangent direction and the normal cannot be defined (treating that axis's gradient as 0 would silently return the degenerate normal cross(dPx,0)=[0,0,0]). It is explicitly rejected with ValueError (fail-closed).

The computation builds 3-D points P with depth_to_organized_points and normalises to unit length the cross product dPx × dPy of the column-direction difference dPx and the row-direction difference dPy from np.gradient (one-sided at the edges). With orient_to_camera=True, pixels with n·(-P) < 0 are flipped so that the normals face the origin (camera). In orthographic mode (fx or fy is None) P=(u,v,d), so the origin lies at depth 0 at the top-left of the image, and note that "facing the camera" means something different from perspective mode. If cx and cy are omitted, the image centre is used. At pixels straddling a depth step (occlusion edge) the cross product picks up the direction of the step and the normal breaks, so remove boundary pixels with occlusion_edges first. Pixels with depth 0 / NaN are not validated, and their normals are undefined. Returns float32 (H,W,3).
